sourceNote: Reviewed all supplied events, E0–E2304. Attribution follows conversational continuity rather than treating every >> marker as a speaker change. Some events combine speakers or contain acknowledgments whose speaker cannot be established from text alone; these are U. The transcript contains apparent transcription errors, preserved in quotations. No audio or external sources were consulted.

teaserSpans.reason: Opening edited montage: passages recur in the substantive discussion at E1541–1569, E1865–1867, E1915–1917, and E2242–2245. E4–E5 is an inserted third-party clip. E29 combines the teaser's ending with the conversational introduction; the whole event is O.

candidates.speaker: A
candidates.quote: surely that scales to to everybody else.
candidates.explanation: A extends his reported experience of wrongdoing weakening felt divine proximity to others, potentially explaining away hiddenness through resistance. Independent grounds for that generalization are missing. However, he accepts the counterexample to a tight moral-character relationship at E532 and E536; E588–589 also rejects individual blame. Blanket protection is therefore unestablished.

candidates.speaker: B
candidates.quote: But I also shouldn't expect to be able to understand this.
candidates.explanation: B recommends a conditional defense that makes apparently gratuitous suffering and uneven revelation unassessable through inaccessible divine reasoning, without specifying limits on that exemption. He supplies a finitude argument, so this is no unsupported slogan. Crucially, E1039–1093 acknowledges its dependence on theism and its damage to positive arguments about God.

candidates.speaker: A
candidates.quote: we are not able to do the costbenefit analysis for all sorts of reasons.
candidates.explanation: A reserves assessment of all creation's suffering to Jesus and treats resurrection as making its cost worthwhile, insulating that assessment from contrary suffering without an accessible justification of the total balance. Scriptural reasoning makes this a protected non-slogan argument. E993–995 disclaims solving evil, and E1094–1113 subsequently limits divine incomprehensibility.

contrasts.speaker: A
contrasts.explanation: The compact affirmation at E1321 summarizes an explicit theological argument: interpersonal love within the Trinity supplies a personal conception of goodness and an alternative to motivation by pure threat. Its premises remain disputable, but the phrase does not replace the reasons supplied at E1295–1320.

contrasts.speaker: B
contrasts.explanation: B explains why the flowering metaphor needs further criteria: retrospective approval risks endorsing whatever happened, while unrestricted change threatens stable moral truth. E2130–2136 then requests an account identifying both development and missteps. The catchphrase summarizes those reasons.
